text: Suppose the index set T is finite and has bounded internal covering number with constant c > 0 and exponent d > 0. Let X satisfy the Kolmogorov moment condition with exponents p > 0 and q > d and constant M. For every δ > 0, the expectation of the supremum of distance(X_s,X_t)^p over s,t in T with distance(s,t) ≤ δ is at most 4^(p+2q+1) M c δ^(q-d) times [4^d max(0, log₂(c δ^(-d) 4^d))^q + Cp(d,p,q)]. Here Cp(d,p,q)=max(1/(2^((q-d)/p)-1)^p, 1/(2^(q-d)-1)). The Kolmogorov condition means that each coordinate pair is a.e. measurable and E[distance(X_s,X_t)^p] ≤ M distance(s,t)^q. The internal covering condition means Nint(ε,T) ≤ c ε^(-d) for scales ε at most the diameter, with cover centers in T.
scope: Finite-set corollary; retain moment and covering-number definitions and Cp context. Label is statement-level and does not certify the proof.
